subject.title: Install ClawHub packages for new Claw agents

question: Should experimental Claws be allowed to install process-wide plugins now, and if so must each install require an explicit Scout- or host-level grant distinct from the individual Claw add consent?
rationale: Code review cannot choose whether one role may mutate executable code shared by sibling agents; that decision defines the permanent authorization, recovery, status, update, and removal contracts.

options.title: Ship Skills First
options.body: Implement workspace-local skill packages and defer process-wide plugin mutation until a shared-host authorization contract exists.

options.title: Require Shared-Host Grant
options.body: Keep plugin support only after adding an explicit host-level grant, verified integrity, ownership visibility, and recovery proof.

options.title: Accept Claw-Level Consent
options.body: Treat the individual Claw add consent as sufficient authorization for shared plugin mutation and explicitly own the cross-agent risk.

recommendation.title: Ship Skills First
recommendation.body: Implement workspace-local skill packages and defer process-wide plugin mutation until a shared-host authorization contract exists.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the assigned reviewer and supplied the package ownership and lifecycle requirements currently shaping this stack.
